name: zclaw
vibe_summary: An ultra-minimalist AI personal assistant that squeezes onto an ESP32 microcontroller with an all-in firmware budget of just 888 KiB. It brings GPIO control, cron scheduling, persistent memory, and custom tools to bare-metal hardware.
best_for: Makers wanting an AI assistant on ESP32 hardware
GPIO and sensor automation via natural language
Learning embedded C + LLM tool integration
avoid_if: You need a rich desktop or server agent runtime
You want a large plugin/skill ecosystem
You need multi-user or team workflows
You are uncomfortable flashing firmware and provisioning credentials
openclaw_advantages: Runs on $5 ESP32 hardware with 888 KiB total firmware
Direct GPIO, I2C, and DHT sensor control built in
No server or PC required; fully self-contained device
Encrypted credential storage in flash with secure flash mode
Supports local LLM backends via Ollama
openclaw_disadvantages: Far smaller tool/skill ecosystem than OpenClaw
Limited to Telegram or web relay chat channels
Constrained by microcontroller RAM and single-device scope
Requires firmware flashing and serial provisioning workflow
No desktop Control UI or multi-agent routing

overview_markdown:
zclaw is a C-based AI personal assistant designed to run entirely on ESP32 microcontrollers, with a strict all-in firmware budget of 888 KiB that includes the ESP-IDF/FreeRTOS runtime, Wi-Fi, TLS, and certificate bundles. Despite the tiny footprint, it supports timezone-aware cron schedules (daily, periodic, one-shot), persistent memory, GPIO control, and user-defined tools composable through natural language. Chat happens over Telegram or a hosted web relay, and credentials (Wi-Fi, LLM API keys, Telegram allowlists) can be provisioned or re-provisioned without reflashing, with an optional secure flash mode for encrypted storage.

Recent development is active and hardware-focused: the v2.13.0 release added DHT sensor and generic I2C tools, hardened tool schemas, and trimmed firmware size to stay within budget. The project supports both cloud LLM backends and local models via Ollama, with compile-time rate limits (100/hour, 1000/day defaults) to control API spend.

Compared to OpenClaw, zclaw trades ecosystem breadth and desktop-class capabilities for extreme minimalism and physical-world access. It is the OpenClaw-adjacent option for makers who want an assistant that can toggle pins, read sensors, and run scheduled automations on a $5 board rather than a full computer.
